newyorker.title: The Family That Built an Empire of Pain

events.title: Brooklyn beginnings
events.description: The Sackler brothers grew up in a Brooklyn immigrant family whose parents ran a grocery store. All three later trained as physicians.

events.title: The physician-to-physician advertising model
events.description: Arthur Sackler joined William Douglas McAdams, an agency focused on pharmaceutical advertising. His later campaigns targeted medical professionals through journals and sales representatives.

events.title: Sackler family enters Purdue
events.description: The brothers acquired Purdue Frederick, then a small drug company. Family-controlled pharmaceutical businesses expanded over subsequent decades.

events.title: The family branches diverge
events.description: Arthur Sackler died nine years before OxyContin launched. His estate sold its stake to Mortimer and Raymond; questions about later estate payments require separate treatment from direct OxyContin management.

events.title: Purdue Pharma incorporated
events.description: The Purdue Pharma entity associated with the later OxyContin rollout was incorporated.

events.title: OxyContin approved and introduced
events.description: OxyContin received FDA approval in 1995 and entered the U.S. market in 1996, with extended-release oxycodone as its active medication.

events.title: Misleading marketing claims
events.description: Purdue Frederick later admitted promoting OxyContin as less addictive and less susceptible to abuse than other pain medicines, despite knowing those claims were false.

events.title: Early state litigation
events.description: West Virginia sued Purdue over alleged illegal marketing; other state actions followed. A lawsuit alleges conduct, and is not by itself a finding of liability.

events.title: Federal misbranding plea
events.description: Purdue Frederick pleaded guilty to felony misbranding; three executives pleaded guilty to misdemeanor misbranding offenses. The company and executives faced financial penalties.

events.title: Billions distributed to the family
events.description: The Supreme Court described approximately $11 billion in distributions from Purdue to Sackler family interests during this period, including funds routed through trusts and companies. Distributions are not identical to spendable after-tax cash.

events.title: OxyContin reformulated
events.description: Purdue introduced abuse-deterrent reformulated OxyContin. The DOJ later described consulting work focused on protecting market share and Purdue’s analysis of declining prescriptions.

events.title: Kentucky settles for $24 million
events.description: Kentucky settled its Purdue lawsuit for $24 million. Some key documents were later unsealed after journalists challenged secrecy.

events.title: Pike County records unsealed
events.description: Following STAT’s legal efforts, Kentucky court records became public, exposing internal plans, emails and marketing materials from as early as the 1990s.

events.title: Purdue files for bankruptcy
events.description: The company entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy under mounting opioid litigation. The settlement and claims process continued for years.

events.title: Additional federal guilty plea
events.description: Purdue pleaded guilty to fraud and kickback conspiracies relating to opioid marketing and anti-diversion obligations. These were corporate guilty pleas, not convictions of individual Sackler family members.

events.title: Museum naming reckoning
events.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that seven named exhibition spaces, including the Temple of Dendur wing, would no longer bear the Sackler name.

events.title: Supreme Court rejects nonconsensual releases
events.description: The Supreme Court held that the bankruptcy code did not permit the proposed broad releases of claims against Sacklers without affected claimants’ consent.

events.title: Revised settlement announced
events.description: States announced a revised $7.4 billion Purdue/Sackler settlement: up to $6.5 billion from the Sackler family and approximately $900 million from Purdue.

events.title: Purdue closes; Knoa takes over
events.description: The settlement took effect. Purdue ceased operations and assets transferred to Knoa Pharma, independently overseen, with Sacklers barred from U.S. opioid commerce.

events.title: Initial settlement payments begin
events.description: California reported more than $1.5 billion paid by Sacklers at implementation, with scheduled subsequent payments. This describes settlement payments, not a full accounting of remaining family assets.

events.title: Publicly reported asset-sale dispute
events.description: Reuters reported a bankruptcy judge denied Richard Sackler’s effort to halt a property sale connected to settlement financing. The atlas records the legal dispute, not private residential details.

people.name: Arthur M. Sackler
people.note: Helped develop pharmaceutical promotion. Died before OxyContin launched. His estate exited direct Purdue ownership; the provenance of a later estate payment was disputed.

people.name: Mortimer Sackler
people.note: A member of the ownership branch that retained Purdue after Arthur’s estate sold its stake.

people.name: Raymond Sackler
people.note: Led Purdue’s pharmaceutical business for decades. His descendants were among later Purdue stakeholders.

people.name: Richard Sackler
people.note: Named in extensive litigation and internal records concerning OxyContin. His 2026 asset-sale litigation was publicly reported. Allegations, admissions and judgments must remain separate.

people.name: Mortimer / Raymond descendants
people.note: Participating family branches settled civil claims and are barred from U.S. opioid sales. No family member had been criminally charged in the cited 2026 reporting.

people.name: Purdue Pharma / Knoa Pharma
people.note: Purdue pleaded guilty to federal crimes and closed. Knoa operates under independent oversight with new public-health obligations.

flows.label: 2008–2016 family distributions
flows.detail: Approximate gross distributions referenced in the Supreme Court opinion; not evidence of identical personal take-home wealth.

flows.label: 2026 settlement total
flows.detail: Up to $6.5B from family members and about $900M from Purdue, spread across a multi-year distribution structure.

flows.label: Family payments at settlement launch
flows.detail: California AG’s report of initial Sackler payments in May 2026. These are not the entire settlement obligation.

flows.label: Kentucky additional settlement (2025)
flows.detail: Kentucky AG announcement; distinct from the earlier $24M state settlement, and one part of broader state recoveries.

flows.label: Arthur estate note paid (1997)
flows.detail: ProPublica traced an estate-related payment. Whether OxyContin profits specifically financed it was disputed; no inference is made here.
